key_insight: Thick single-crystal lead-halide perovskites enable bright, coherent, ultra-broadband four-wave mixing without phase matching or angular alignment, thanks to their very large intrinsic third-order nonlinearity.
engineering_relevance: This points to a compact, alignment-free bulk material platform for ultrafast frequency conversion and broadband nonlinear photonic devices.
method: Used near- and mid-infrared femtosecond pulses in thick single-crystal lead-halide perovskites.
Measured four-wave mixing output across a wide continuous tuning range without dispersion or alignment optimization.
Used time-resolved measurements to localize emission near crystal surfaces.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports bright, coherent, highly collimated emission over an exceptionally wide continuous tuning range, supported by time-resolved evidence that the interaction is surface-localized.
watch_item: Performance may depend on surface-localized emission in thick crystals, so device integration and reproducibility could be sensitive to crystal quality and surface conditions.
paper_title: Alignment-free ultra-broadband parametric frequency conversion in lead-halide perovskites
